title: Unclutter session bridge and introduce preset retry profiles across py/ts/go
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Context: multiple SDK consumers asked for a simpler, more discoverable session API surface (less indirection between 'Session', 'SessionBridge', and lower-level PullStream/PullIterator types) plus clearer, opinionated retry presets tuned for latency-first vs throughput-first workloads. This PR centralizes a small session facade across the three SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go), provides compact adapters to the existing PullStream/legacy connector, and introduces two named retry presets (latency_sensitive, throughput_sensitive) that are exposed from each SDK and wired into the client config. Motivation: reduce onboarding friction, minimize token-level latency surprises from overbroad batching backoffs, and provide a consistent migration path for older integrations.

What I changed (summary): consolidated session factory surface into a lightweight facade (SessionFacade) in each SDK, added a thin compatibility adapter that maps legacy PullStream semantics to the new typed async generator / iterator surface, exported two retry preset names with clearly documented tradeoffs, synchronized version pins for the three SDKs (py 0.23.1 -> 0.23.2; ts 1.14.0 -> 1.14.1; go 0.9.7 -> 0.9.8), and added end-to-end smoke tests that exercise stream resume + credential refresh scenarios. Important: the PR keeps the legacy types but marks the previous SessionBridge constructor as deprecated with a runtime shim; no immediate breaking changes.

Notes on behavior and compatibility: the new SessionFacade wraps the existing internal runtime connector and provides a consistent async iterator/stream API: Python yields async generator objects, TypeScript exposes AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>, Go returns a typed channel + Close semantics. The legacy SessionBridge constructor that accepted a raw PullStream is still present but annotated with @deprecated and logs a single warning at first use; the compatibility adapter will translate older pattern-based pull semantics to the new iterator-driven flow for a best-effort no-code migration.

Retry presets: two named profiles are introduced and exported from each SDK. They are small, opinionated bundles of backoff parameters and concurrency hints intended to cover the two most common production needs without forcing teams to hand-tune: 
- latency_sensitive: short initial backoff, minimal max backoff, conservative concurrency to reduce token-delay tail latency. Best when latency SLOs matter.
- throughput_sensitive: longer backoff windows, higher batching/concurrency allowed, favors token cost reduction over tight latency SLOs.

Observability: the presets wire diagnostic labels into request telemetry (retry.preset=<name>) so platform dashboards can correlate incident signals with retry strategy choice. The change also adds a short trace span around the adapter conversion to help debug resume/handshake failures.

Testing and CI: added unit tests for the presets and adapter conversion; integration smoke tests run against a local runtime harness that simulates KV cache warm/cold and token refresh. CI was flaky initially on Windows/Go due to a time.Sleep-based test; I replaced that with a deterministic mock in the final commits. The full CI matrix is green on merge.

Review summary / discussion (short): the reviewers asked for clearer naming (SessionFacade vs SessionFactory) and explicit migration examples. I adjusted names and added a short snippet in docs showing both the new pattern and the migration shim. We debated exporting the presets as strings vs typed enums; consensus was to export them as well-known string constants for language ergonomics but include typed helpers where idiomatic (TS enums, Go constants, Python literal types).

Merge outcome: squash-merged on 2026-02-17 after final CI run and a follow-up tidy commit to fix a linter complaint in TS. Release notes entry prepared and version bumps staged for the next SDK release cycle.

migration_snippet:
Python (new):
from redwood import SessionFacade, retries
s = SessionFacade.from_api_key(KEY, retry_preset=retries.latency_sensitive)
async for chunk in s.stream('hello'):
    handle(chunk)

Legacy shim (will log once):
bridge = SessionBridge(legacy_stream)  # still works but deprecated
